text:
maria: Hey team — preauth POC for FinLedger hitting 429s during parallel CSV->embeds ingest. Sales says customer sees tokens on their invoice but requests are getting blocked. Can someone help triage? tenant=finledger-123 route=ingest-emb

aj: @maria got it. Can you paste a raw 429 response (headers + body) and confirm which endpoints are used (embeddings vs chat/generate)?

maria: Paste of a single failed request (redacted):
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000450
X-Route-Limit: 300
X-Route-Remaining: 0
{
  "error": { "message": "rate limit exceeded", "code": 429 }
}
We call /v1/embeddings in a tight loop (concurrency ~40) from a small pool of clients.

aj: Looks like tenant-level limit 1200 and route cap 300. Route bucket exhausted. The billing token question: billing is metered on accepted requests; 429s should not be billed. Do you have request IDs for a couple of hits so engineering can check metering logs?

maria: One request-id I pulled: r-8f3b2a. Customer is attaching invoice line that shows ~35k tokens that they claim were from the POC window. They started at 9:10am UTC when we saw the 429s.

tim: quick context — we recently enabled per-route softcaps for preauth/trial tenants to protect shared pools. That explains X-Route-Limit lower than tenant limit. Softcaps can drop requests (429) but shouldn't appear on billing. If invoice shows billed tokens, either metering double-counted or those tokens were from earlier successful requests.

kevin: From acct side — customer says charges correspond exactly to the timeframe when they saw 429s, so they think we're billing for attempted requests. We need evidence: request+metering logs mapping to billable events.

aj: Maria can you run this curl from a failing client and paste headers:
curl -I -H "Authorization: Bearer <key>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings
Sample expected headers to copy: X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining, X-RateLimit-Reset, X-Route-Limit, X-Route-Remaining, x-request-id

maria: Ran it, posting output:
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
x-request-id: r-8f3b2a
X-RateLimit-Limit: 1200
X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0
X-RateLimit-Reset: 1700000450
X-Route-Limit: 300
X-Route-Remaining: 0

aj: Ok that confirms enforcement on the route. Next steps: (1) engineering will check metering pipeline for r-8f3b2a to confirm billing event, (2) we can temporarily raise the route softcap for finledger-123 or whitelist the route for the POC, (3) recommend client add jitter/backoff to the ingest to avoid hitting route bucket.

quota-bot: Quota change requested by tim: tenant=finledger-123 route=ingest-emb action=softcap_increase pct=+60 expires=2029-01-10T00:00:00Z status=pending

tim: Applied temporary increase while we confirm billing. @kevin you should see no new billing for blocked requests; if accounting already shows charges, we'll reconcile with the invoice credit if needed.

maria: After quota bump the pipeline recovered immediately, concurrency steady and errors dropped to 0 within 90s. Customer re-ran their bulk and saw successful responses. I'll attach request-ids for the period to your PM ticket, @aj. Thanks all :thumbsup:

aj: I'll audit metering logs for r-8f3b2a and the window 2029-04-05T09:05:00Z–09:20:00Z and report back. If there's a billing bug we'll credit the customer.

kevin: Thanks folks — please keep me posted, I'll prep a one-time credit if we confirm misbilling.

maria: Closing loop: customer happy with throughput after bump. We'll add backoff guidance to the POC docs and recommend per-route concurrency limits in the onboarding checklist.
